messages:
Alex: Heads up — after the firmware push to BMC on rack g-12 (us-central1) last night, ~25 GPU nodes are hitting a quiet reboot loop around kernel handoff; provisioning jobs keep timing out on iSCSI init.
Sara: Ah — are we seeing secure boot flips or UEFI vars changed?
Mike: Yup, confirmed on ~8 nodes the secure-boot flag got set to 'Enabled' during the BMC write.
Mike: quick snip of serial:```
[  12.345678] PCI: Probing PCI bridge to detect IO/APIC routing...
[  12.456789] iSCSI: login timeout after 60s
[  12.456800] kernel: reboot: Restarting system
```
Ivan: Can we SSM into a node or use IPMI SOL and check kernel cmdline? If secure boot is toggled kernel modules may be rejected.
Alex: IPMI SOL shows kernel gets to initramfs then the iSCSI mount fails and it reboots. Tried `ipmitool sol activate` -> dumps same loop.
Julia: Runbook step: rollback BMC image to previous SHA on affected racks, then force a cold power cycle. We should canary 2 nodes first.
Mike: Agreed. Doing canary now on g-12-03 and g-12-07. Rolling back to bmc-fw@2026-02-11-0.9.2.
ops-bot: [alert] Deploy job #1258 failed health checks on 25 nodes in us-central1; automatically paused further BMC rollouts.
Alex: Immediate impact: GPU capacity for batch jobs in us-central1 dropped ~18% — backlog growing; scheduler has started evicting low-priority preemptible workloads. Estimated cost delta: more cross-region bursts ~ $220/hr if we failover to eu-west.
Sara: Can we avoid cross-region bursts? Maybe expand dedicated capacity in us-west for 2-3 hours while we remediate.
Ivan: I'll coordinate with capacity team. Also adding a temporary routing rule: prefer nodes not in rack g-12 for new provisioning until BMC rollback completes.
Julia: Note for postmortem: why did BMC image set secure-boot? Public vs. private build flag mismatch?
Mike: Found a CI artifact mismatch — build metadata had an env var `ENABLE_SECURE_BOOT=1` for that release. Root cause candidate.
Liam: Putting a short incident thread in #incidents and pinging infra oncall.
Alex: Timeline: canary started 4311223380; if stable by +10m we'll proceed rack-by-rack.
Sara: If rollback doesn't fix kernel module loading we may need to disable secure boot via UEFI variable in the BIOS as fallback (manual, slower).
Ivan: I'll prep the manual BIOS fallback instructions and estimate 20m/node hands-on.
Julia: Thanks — keep notes of nodes that required manual BIOS change for RCA.
Mike: Canary nodes are stable for now. iSCSI mounts succeeded after rollback.
Alex: Good. Proceeding with staged rollback. I'll post updates here. :thumbsup:
